tallyNote: Seven distinct objections. C2T2-BOTH-01 is one objection affecting D-019 and D-020 and is counted once in each per-entry mustFix tally; summing per-entry counts therefore yields eight, not seven. D-018 receives CONSENT: its single finding is a NOTE, and no MUST-FIX or SHOULD-FIX against it survives the start bytes.
summary: Every turn-1 finding I raised is LANDED-VERIFIED in the new bytes, and the repairs are substantive rather than cosmetic — the closed consumption set is gone with Route A restored, the bundle is split into four severable entries with per-entry revert clauses, the SF-3 conflict is not merely struck but explicitly negated, and the 'cannot gate' prohibition now matches D-002's T2-02 trade. Both internal citations the turn-2 draft newly introduces re-measure clean, including one (D-006 turn-2 NOTE-03) that binds the entry tighter than either reviewer asked. The residual defects are new and concentrate in the split itself: D-019 selects Route B for DR-005, which IS the V10/custody and G19 row, while severable D-020 names V10/custody and G19 by name as staying Route A — an undisclosed overlap between two entries that can be adopted independently. Separately, neither D-019 nor D-020 names the owning V1 authority who will record each Route B disposition, though condition 1's own text requires 'the owning V1 authority records' it and D-021 does name owners for the Route A lane. D-017's Route C now carries a gloss that narrows D-001's third route to a recording surface the product-disposition process does not always use. D-021's seven-step pin no longer counts steps.

objections.claim: D-019 selects Route B for DR-005, which is the V10/custody and G19 row, while severable D-020 names V10/custody and G19 by name as remaining on Route A. The two entries make routing claims over the same underlying semantics without disclosing the overlap, and either can be adopted without the other.
objections.evidence: File 08 (a3e37102991b80502aa1f9fb1affe2011859917b8ce1477a93f494485b9161b7) line 38 defines DR-005 as 'V10/custody and G19 durable-authoritative mechanism remain unresolved', owned by 'Evidence, storage, operability authorities', pinned to 'freeze ... §3 EVIDENCE/TM/OPERABILITY; operability.v10 ... G19 limitation'. Draft L258-264 selects Route B for DR-005 among the four. Draft L328-330 (D-020 Decision 2) states: 'Full TM closure stays Route A on the authoritative-MVP path: V10/custody, G19 demonstration, publication block, and TM's final disposition remain required before any authoritative-closure claim.' D-019's own severability boundary at L252-254 asserts DR-003 is 'a different fact' from the four — but DR-005's own source pin includes freeze §3 TM, and its subject matter is exactly the V10/custody and G19 pair D-020 reserves to Route A. The two are reconcilable only by reading D-019's selection as preview-scoped and D-020's reservation as authoritative-scoped, which is almost certainly the intent — but no sentence in either entry says so, and the header at L8-9 makes them independently consentable. Adopting D-019 without D-020 leaves DR-005 selected for Route B with no entry stating that V10/custody and G19 remain owed on the authoritative path; adopting D-020 without D-019 leaves its V10/G19 sentence describing a row whose route was not selected.
objections.proposedFix: Add one sentence to D-019's 'Why these four rise and fall together' disclosing the overlap, e.g.: 'DR-005 is the row that carries V10/custody and G19. Selecting Route B for it is preview-scoped only; the full V10/custody and G19 demonstration remains owed on the authoritative path regardless of whether D-020 is adopted, and this entry does not discharge it.' Mirror the cross-reference in D-020 Decision 2 so neither entry's adoption in isolation leaves the other half unstated.

objections.claim: Applies to D-019 and D-020. Neither entry names the owning V1 authority who will record each Route B disposition, although D-001 condition 1's own text conditions the alternative on 'the owning V1 authority records' it, and DR-204 already ruled that a coordinator-composed discharge is unlawful for a graded disposition. D-021 names owners for the Route A lane, which makes the omission on the Route B side conspicuous rather than incidental.
objections.evidence: File 08's readiness condition 1 reads: 'DR-001 through DR-011 are SATISFIED or THE OWNING V1 AUTHORITY records an explicit, scoped, reviewed pre-blueprint disposition that names what may be designed without pretending the blocked semantics are settled.' D-019 L267 says only 'This entry writes none of those dispositions' and L249-250 calls them 'later isolated entries, each with its own reviewed bytes'; D-020 L332-333 says the scoped threat model is 'a later isolated artifact with its own independent review'. Neither names an author or authority. File 08 records distinct owners per row: DR-002 'Evidence authority + V1 coordinator'; DR-004 'Evidence/retention authority'; DR-005 'Evidence, storage, operability authorities'; DR-008 'Product owner (sfbreen) for posture; evidence/retention authority for contract'; DR-003 'Threat-model authority + V1 coordinator'. By contrast D-021 step 7 (L425-426) does state ownership for Route A: those rows 'remain owned by the surface owners D-001 already names.' The asymmetry matters because 'later isolated entries' in this corpus are coordinator acts in COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, and file 08's DR-204 row records the governing precedent: a coordinator-composed discharge 'is unlawful for this grade' where the disposition requires independent standing. If the five dispositions are authored as coordinator entries without the named owning authority recording them, they will not satisfy condition 1's own wording and the Route B selection will have bought nothing.
objections.proposedFix: Add to D-019 Decision 2 and D-020 Decision 3 a sentence naming, per row, the owning V1 authority from file 08 that must record the disposition, and stating that the coordinator selects the route but does not hold the recording authority. If the coordinator intends to act as or on behalf of an owning authority under D-000 delegation, say so explicitly and record how that avoids the DR-204 defect.

objections.claim: D-017 restores D-001's three routes but glosses Route C as 'recorded as a D-000 entry', which narrows it to a recording surface the product-disposition process does not always use. In an entry that claims to be a pure restatement adding 'no fourth route and no new closed consumption set', a narrowing of the third route is the same defect class turn 1 objected to, at lower magnitude.
objections.evidence: Draft L94-95: 'Route C — a product decision through the product-disposition process, RECORDED AS A D-000 ENTRY.' D-001 §3 at COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md L154-155 reads only: '(C) a product decision through the product-disposition process.' The trailing clause is added. It is not always true: the product-disposition process writes to product-dispositions.v1.json, a separate authority surface. File 00's authority-layers table lists 'product-dispositions.v1.json — Product-authority choices such as P-1, P-2, G3, and CD-RT-5', and file 08's DR-008 row pins the CD-RT-5 posture to 'product bbe24527f732f9c265f9cf71b988303a326e45fec0c6adb0d934536d515d6017#$.decisions["CD-RT-5"]', decided by the product owner on 2026-08-05 — not as a D-000 coordinator entry. The narrowing is live, not hypothetical: DR-117, the product-boundary successor to P-1/P-2/G3, is owned by 'Product owner' and pinned to that same product packet, so its successor plausibly lands there rather than in COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md. Under D-017 as written, that route is mis-described. D-017's decision-type paragraph (L66-70) asserts the entry 'restates rules already present in ... D-001's three closure routes.'
objections.proposedFix: Strike ', recorded as a D-000 entry' so Route C reads as D-001 wrote it, or replace with an accurate disjunction: 'recorded either in the product-disposition packet by the product authority or, where the coordinator decides on the user's behalf under D-000, as a D-000 entry.'

objections.claim: The 'count-pinned at seven steps' pin no longer counts steps. Item 6 is a disclaimer rather than work the coordinator attempts, and item 7 carries two distinct acts, so the enumeration covers one non-step and eight acts under a pin of seven. Both defects were introduced by the turn-1 repairs, not inherited.
objections.evidence: Draft L385-388 sets the frame: 'The coordinator attempts remaining D-001 work in this order (count-pinned at seven steps...).' Item 6 (L416-421) reads 'This entry does not recalculate file 08's condition-2 or condition-4 sets...' — a statement about the entry, not work to attempt; it is the correct repair of C2-D018-02 but it is no longer a step. Item 7 (L422-432) carries two independent acts: the standing parallel Route A lane ('Standing parallel Route A lane, starts now... continues until those rows are SATISFIED or lawfully disposed'), and the execute-file-08 instruction that stood alone as turn-1 step 7 ('After the then-current file 08 is the only live readiness plan, execute it until D-001's five conditions hold and condition 5 authorizes docs/v2/implementation/'). The connective compounds the problem: file 08 is ALREADY the only live readiness plan — D-017 Decision 1-2 and file 08's own paragraph both say so — so 'After [it] is the only live readiness plan' states a condition that already holds and reads as a sequencing gate that is not one. Turn 1 objected to count-pin honesty at C2-D017-02; this is the same class recurring in the entry that inherited the sequence.
objections.proposedFix: Move item 6 out of the numbered list into a standalone 'What this entry does not do' sentence, split item 7's execute-file-08 clause into its own step, and re-pin the count to whatever the enumeration then holds. Replace the temporal connective with a plain statement, e.g. 'File 08 remains the only live readiness plan throughout; execute it until D-001's five conditions hold and condition 5 authorizes docs/v2/implementation/.'

objections.claim: The inseparability argument paraphrases D-002's deferral reason as a causal claim, and the byte-accurate reason is both different and stronger for the argument being made.
objections.evidence: Draft L242-244: 'D-002 deferred DR-106, DR-109, and DR-113 wholly BECAUSE the preview ships no authoritative sealed closure, no replay, and no evidence custody.' D-002's actual bytes in COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md give a different stated reason, adjacent in the same State paragraph: 'DR-106, DR-109 and DR-113 are deferred WHOLLY: their acceptance-evidence cells all begin with applied DR-002..008 successors, and DR-113's "purge half" would have designed the typed purge result DR-007 expressly forbids inventing.' The exclusion of authoritative closure and the wholly-deferral are adjacent claims that the draft joins causally. The byte-accurate reason directly links DR-106/109/113 to DR-002..008, which is precisely the linkage D-019's 'one fact' argument needs; paraphrasing it away substitutes a weaker warrant for a stronger one that is available in the corpus.
objections.proposedFix: Quote D-002's stated reason instead: 'D-002 deferred DR-106, DR-109 and DR-113 wholly because their acceptance-evidence cells all begin with applied DR-002..008 successors. Those successors are exactly the rows selected here.'

objections.claim: Step 1 forward-references step 7 inside a list whose preamble declares an order, leaving the enumeration's ordering semantics ambiguous.
objections.evidence: Draft L390-391: '1. Isolated product decisions, in parallel with the Route A lane in step 7's standing instruction.' The preamble at L385-386 says 'The coordinator attempts remaining D-001 work in this order.' A first item that runs in parallel with a seventh, plus items 4 and 5 that disclaim gating the seventh, means the list is not an order in any strict sense. This is not a false statement and the parallelism is exactly what ADV-D018-T1-03 required; it is a presentational residue of retrofitting a parallel lane into an ordered list.
objections.proposedFix: Optional. If tightened, restructure as two named lanes — a preview lane holding items 1-5 and a standing Route A lane — with sequencing stated only within each lane. That would also dissolve C2T2-D021-01.

objections.claim: The affirmative half of the narrowed gating clause is correct but uncited, while the negative half carries a byte citation.
objections.evidence: Draft L178-182: 'The slice does produce a verdict and a D9 exit. What it cannot produce is a durable authoritative record of having gated, and it has no baseline/ratchet. That is D-002's T2-02 trade (COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md D-002 State paragraph).' The citation covers the trade, i.e. the negative half. The affirmative claim that the slice produces a verdict and a D9 exit is true — I verified it independently from D-002's condition-2 affected-row set, which includes DR-123 (file 08: mandatory stable human and machine output, non-interactive CI, exits), and its condition-4 required-gate set, which includes G17 for analyze (file 08's G17 row requires the advertised SARIF projection to carry 'Run/Finding IDs, Coverage, verdict, truncation, artifact references') — but the entry does not name that basis. Since Decision 3 binds all later prose, a reader repairing a future overclaim will want the affirmative half anchored too.
objections.proposedFix: Add the basis inline: '(verdict and exit follow from DR-123 and DR-G17, both in D-002's own condition-2 and condition-4 sets).'

The application is accurate and conservative — NOTE-03 addressed a file-08 row-status label, and the draft extends it by analogy to an assurance-stage vocabulary, which binds the entry more tightly than the source requires. Axis 1, residual bundling: each of the five entries carries its own revert clause naming its own commit and stating what revert leaves standing (L143-144, L225-227, L309-311, L366-367, L471-472). D-019 is the only entry bundling multiple acts, and it states an inseparability argument, which turn 1's proposed fix contemplated. The argument's soundness is assessed at C2T2-D019-01 and C2T2-D019-02.

Axis 3, D-020 scoped TM: the entry does NOT skip TM, does NOT waive V10/custody/G19/publication block, and does NOT mark DR-003 SATISFIED. Decision 2 (L328-331) reserves all four to Route A on the authoritative path in terms; Decision 3 (L332-333) withholds the artifact; Decision 4 (L334-336) limits discharge to preview scope and authorizes no blueprint; the closing list (L483) states 'Do not skip TM; D-020 selects a scoped model, not an absence.' The turn-1 closing item 'Do not waive DR-003' was correctly replaced rather than dropped, because D-020 now scopes DR-003 instead of leaving it untouched.

Axis 4, Route A parallelism: substantively real, not a flourish. Verified at four independent sites — step 7 'starts now' / 'not sequenced behind steps 4 or 5' (L422-427); steps 4 and 5 each 'does not gate the Route A lane' (L411, L414-415); step 1 'in parallel with the Route A lane' (L390-391); step 3 in-flight successors 'are not paused for "finish the register"' (L407-408). Ownership is assigned by reference to D-001's named surface owners (L425-426). The residual is presentational and is raised at C2T2-D021-01/02.

Axis 6, silent D-001 or D-002 amendment: none found beyond the Route C gloss at C2T2-D017-01. D-021 step 6 now affirmatively defers to SF-3 rather than constraining it. No entry quotes D-001's five conditions, so the turn-1 paraphrase-as-verbatim trap is not sprung. D-002's command, language-role, platform, deferral, identity-ride, condition-2 and condition-4 sets are untouched; D-018 Decision 2 and D-019 Decision 2 both say so and neither contradicts itself elsewhere.

Axis 7, Route B as blueprint authorization: fully repaired. D-019 Decision 3 and D-020 Decision 4 both state Route B authorizes no blueprint, conditions 2-5 remain independently required, and condition 5 remains the sole authorization for docs/v2/implementation/. D-018 Decision 5 repeats the condition-5 point. The closing list opens with 'Do not authorize docs/v2/implementation/.'

Axis 8, count pins: D-019's four-member pin is arithmetically correct and its members match file 08's row IDs; 'integration half' remains file 08's own phrase (line 41, 'posture half closed, integration half open'), so D-019 L265-266's disclaimer is accurate. D-021's seven-step pin fails on composition, raised at C2T2-D021-01. No 'row'/'re-open' language survives on any coordinator entry.

Axis 10, vacuous caveats: recomputed the closing eight-item list against the draft body. All eight hold. 'Do not waive DR-006 or DR-007' is supported by D-019 Decision 2. 'Do not write any Route B disposition' is supported by D-019 Decision 2 and D-020 Decision 3. 'Do not decide parallel-product posture or DR-117' is supported by D-021 step 1 and D-018 Decision 6. Each entry's 'Readiness effect: Zero' is true — no entry moves a file 08 status cell, and file 08 re-measures unchanged at a3e37102 after review.
D-018's four-rides-on-DR-006, one-on-DR-007 parenthetical is carried forward at D-019 L269-270 and remains correct against D-002's Identity-dependencies section.
